title: Medicare Advantage vs Original Medicare: The Plain Truth
bigPicture: Original Medicare lets you use any doctor or hospital that takes Medicare. Medicare Advantage usually limits you to a plan network but adds a yearly limit on what you pay.
whatYouNeedToKnow: Original Medicare lets you use any doctor or hospital that accepts Medicare, anywhere in the U.S. Medicare Advantage generally limits you to the plan's network and service area for non-emergency care.
In most cases you do not need a referral to see a specialist with Original Medicare. With Medicare Advantage you may need one.
Original Medicare needs a separate Part D drug plan, which has its own premium. Most Medicare Advantage plans include drug coverage.
Medicare Advantage plans may offer extras such as some vision, hearing, and dental services. Original Medicare does not cover routine eye exams or most dental care.
Medicare Advantage has a yearly out-of-pocket limit. Original Medicare has no yearly limit unless you have supplemental coverage.
Medicare Advantage may require prior approval for some services. Original Medicare usually does not.
Medigap works only with Original Medicare. You cannot buy Medigap if you have Medicare Advantage.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Assuming your doctors are in a Medicare Advantage plan's network without checking.
Comparing only the monthly premium and ignoring copays, deductibles, and the yearly out-of-pocket limit.
Forgetting that emergency and urgent care are covered even from providers outside the plan's network.
actionSteps: List your doctors, medicines, and preferred hospitals.
Compare Original Medicare and Medicare Advantage on Medicare.gov using that list.
Check whether each plan you are considering covers your doctors and your medicines.
Review your coverage again each year, since plans can change.
